scenarios.name: Unsupported features have no usable action
scenarios.given: a platform reports a feature unsupported by its OS or hardware
scenarios.then: the unsupported feature has no selectable/configurable or execute action, its compatibility reason stays visible, and settings may still offer supported alternatives

manual.reason: The shared readiness policy alone does not prove that native iOS/iPadOS, watchOS and macOS adapters or controls apply it.
steps: For each affected platform, verify its native capability adapter against actual OS/hardware, permission and model readiness.
Inspect rendered controls and verify supported alternatives; Watch remote controls also require connectivity and matching protocol capability.
Refresh after foreground/settings/connectivity changes and preserve provider choices; keep simulator and physical acceptance separate.

scenarios.name: Setup remains explicit before execution
scenarios.given: a supported feature has denied microphone access or requires summary model/provider setup
scenarios.then: configuration remains available with an actionable reason but execution stays blocked

scenarios.name: Gate Watch local and remote recording independently
scenarios.given: the paired phone is unreachable, incompatible, unchecked or cannot transcribe, or Watch microphone/resources are unavailable
scenarios.when: recording controls appear or their runtime status changes
scenarios.then: remote Start is blocked with the actual recovery reason, reachable Stop remains usable, and independent local Watch recording depends only on its microphone and resources while offline audio remains queued

manual.reason: Core tests execute the policy compiled into Watch; simulator rendering and paired physical delivery remain separate.
steps: Build and inspect Watch simulator controls offline and with a denied microphone profile.
Verify real paired-device capability refresh and Stop, disconnected local recording and later audio sync before embedding Watch for distribution.

scenarios.name: Offer compatible Mac AI and transcription choices before capture
scenarios.given: Mac runtime reports unavailable Apple Intelligence, a denied microphone or unsupported selected speech engine/language
scenarios.when: settings and listening controls are displayed or refreshed
scenarios.then: unavailable Apple selection is refused without changing the saved provider, AI execution and listening are gated independently, and blocked recording explains permissions or compatible engine/language alternatives before microphone activation

manual.reason: Core tests execute the native Mac control policy; framework capability mapping, rendered UI and actual audio require installed-app acceptance.
steps: Inspect Settings AI and transcription options against actual framework availability; preserve stored choices and keys.
Verify disabled Start and recovery for an unavailable profile, enabled Start on supported hardware and usable Stop after a capability change.
Verify real microphone and system-audio OTHERS transcript on a supported Mac and preserve source-matched screenshots; clean only the completed Dev session.

scenarios.name: Cancel pending Mac Start across readiness and permission waits
scenarios.given: Start is waiting for device capabilities or microphone permission
scenarios.when: the window closes, Stop or New cancels it, or its task is cancelled
scenarios.then: late success cannot request more permissions or create capture, duplicate Start is refused, and an obsolete completion cannot cancel a newer conversation start; a delayed permission denial never publishes an error into a new conversation

scenarios.name: Keep release visuals explicit about simulated compatible hardware
scenarios.given: release screenshots use a synthetic conversation and supported recording profile on a simulator
scenarios.when: the release fixture opens the real workspace views
scenarios.then: Start is enabled from the explicit fixture profile without requesting microphone permission; the normal simulator app still explains unsupported live recording
